results.name: near_minus_mid_gradient
results.description: Yes rate for non-example targets 1-5 away from the nearest example minus yes rate for targets 6-20 away; observed > null means people show a steeper numeric-proximity (similarity) gradient than the model produces, observed < null a flatter one.
results.code:
# name: near_minus_mid_gradient
# description: Yes rate for non-example targets 1-5 away from the nearest example minus yes rate for targets 6-20 away; observed > null means people show a steeper numeric-proximity (similarity) gradient than the model produces, observed < null a flatter one.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    mind = np.nanmin(np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    a = (mind >= 1) & (mind <= 5)
    b = (mind >= 6) & (mind <= 20)
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: outside_range_minus_inside_gap
results.description: For multi-example sets, yes rate for non-example targets within 10 outside the example range [min,max] minus yes rate for non-example targets strictly inside the range; observed > null (less negative) means people extend generalization beyond the example range more than the model's interval hypotheses do (softer range edges).
results.code:
# name: outside_range_minus_inside_gap
# description: For multi-example sets, yes rate for non-example targets within 10 outside the example range [min,max] minus yes rate for non-example targets strictly inside the range; observed > null (less negative) means people extend generalization beyond the example range more than the model's interval hypotheses do (softer range edges).
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    k = (~np.isnan(ex)).sum(axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    lo = np.nanmin(ex, axis=1); hi = np.nanmax(ex, axis=1)
    notex = ~(ex == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    inside = (k >= 2) & notex & (t > lo) & (t < hi)
    outside = (k >= 2) & notex & (((t < lo) & (t >= lo - 10)) | ((t > hi) & (t <= hi + 10)))
    if inside.sum() == 0 or outside.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[outside].mean() - r[inside].mean())

results.name: early_minus_late_yes_rate
results.description: Yes rate on trials with trial_index < 90 minus yes rate on trials with trial_index >= 90; observed > null means people say yes more early in the session than the time-invariant model produces (a drift the model lacks).

results.name: example_target_yes_rate
results.description: Yes rate when the target is itself one of the shown examples; observed < null means the model over-produces "yes" for already-seen examples (people are not certain about given members).

results.name: shared_last_digit_yes_rate
results.description: Among sets of 2+ examples that all end in the same digit, yes rate for non-example targets ending in that digit; observed < null means the model over-produces "ends in d" rule generalization (people endorse last-digit rules less than the model infers), observed > null the reverse.
results.code:
# name: shared_last_digit_yes_rate
# description: Among sets of 2+ examples that all end in the same digit, yes rate for non-example targets ending in that digit; observed < null means the model over-produces "ends in d" rule generalization (people endorse last-digit rules less than the model infers), observed > null the reverse.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    valid = ~np.isnan(ex)
    k = valid.sum(axis=1)
    last = np.mod(ex, 10)
    first_last = last[:, 0]
    alls = np.where(valid, last == first_last[:, None], True).all(axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    notex = ~(ex == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    m = (k >= 2) & alls & notex & (np.mod(t, 10) == first_last)
    if m.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(df["rating"].to_numpy()[m].mean())

results.name: far_target_yes_rate
results.description: Yes rate among targets more than 20 away from every example and sharing no last digit with any example; observed > null means the model under-produces diffuse/random "yes" to unrelated targets (missing lapse/broad generalization).
results.code:
# name: far_target_yes_rate
# description: Yes rate among targets more than 20 away from every example and sharing no last digit with any example; observed > null means the model under-produces diffuse/random "yes" to unrelated targets (missing lapse/broad generalization).
def test_statistic(df):
    k = df["number_set"].str.count(",") + 1
    ex = df["number_set"].str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    d = np.abs(ex - t[:, None])
    mind = np.nanmin(d, axis=1)
    lastmatch = np.nansum((np.mod(ex, 10) == np.mod(t, 10)[:, None]) & ~np.isnan(ex), axis=1) > 0
    m = (mind > 20) & ~lastmatch
    if m.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(df["rating"].to_numpy()[m].mean())

results.name: lag1_response_agreement
results.description: Proportion of consecutive trials (trial_index increments by 1) whose responses are equal; observed > null means responses are more sequentially dependent (perseveration/streaks) than the model's independent per-trial responses produce.

results.name: single_example_yes_rate
results.description: Yes rate on trials with exactly one example (non-example targets); observed > null means the model generalizes too narrowly from a single example, observed < null too broadly.
results.code:
# name: single_example_yes_rate
# description: Yes rate on trials with exactly one example (non-example targets); observed > null means the model generalizes too narrowly from a single example, observed < null too broadly.
def test_statistic(df):
    k = (df["number_set"].astype(str).str.count(",") + 1).to_numpy()
    ex = df["number_set"].str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    notex = ~(ex == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    m = (k == 1) & notex
    if m.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(df["rating"].to_numpy()[m].mean())
